main.headline: Google to cut Search access for schools that block its AI
main.summary: Google announced new AI tools for classrooms and said schools can turn off its AI features. Google's education vice president, Chris Phillips, told the New York Times that Search and AI are integrated, so schools that ban AI will lose Search access for students. Google also said access to Gemini and Search AI features will be off for K-12 student accounts until administrators turn them on. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and former FTC Chair Lina Khan accused Google of using its search monopoly to push AI into schools.

main.headline: Voters approve dozens of data center restrictions in midterm elections
main.summary: Of 41 data center measures across 10 states, about two dozen that restrict or block development appeared to pass, according to Axios, citing Ballotpedia. The Verge counts 45 local measures, with 33 restricting development as of Wednesday. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the Texas governor's race on a platform of keeping a data center construction moratorium until the state passes new rules. Texas accounts for 41% of new US data center capacity in 2028, according to SemiAnalysis.

main.headline: OpenAI to acquire developer tooling startup Pierre Computer
main.summary: OpenAI announced plans to acquire Pierre Computer, which runs a cloud service where AI agents store code. Terms were not disclosed, and The Decoder reports the deal needs regulatory approval. Two of Pierre's open-source libraries, Trees and Diffs, already power OpenAI's Codex interface. OpenAI will keep them open source and plans to integrate Pierre's paid code hosting into Codex.

main.headline: Anthropic releases FlashProve, a prototype to verify which model answered
main.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source research prototype that uses cryptographic proofs to show a response came from a specific AI model without revealing its weights. The Decoder reports it generates proofs at about 110 tokens per second on one H100 GPU, with overhead of roughly 70x to 95x over normal inference. It proves only contexts up to 1,024 tokens and works only when the model picks the most likely next token.

europe_brief.headline: UK proptech Supa raises £21 million seed round for AI property management
europe_brief.summary: Supa raised £21 million in equity and debt, with the equity round co-led by 2150 and OpenOcean. The company buys local block management firms and adds AI to automate administrative work; it manages about 20,000 homes through seven firms.
item_titles: Supa raises £21M in seed funding to transform UK residential block management

europe_brief.headline: Aker CEO calls Microsoft's exit from Nscale deal a "minor contract"
europe_brief.summary: Aker, which owns about 23% of Nscale, said Microsoft's cancellation was expected and small relative to Nscale's contract portfolio. Microsoft cancelled after its Essex data center was found unlikely to have power until after 2030, tech.eu reports.
item_titles: Microsoft "minor contract" loss, says Nscale key investor

finance_brief.headline: Binance says hackers used fake job interviews and internal AI tool in $6.3 billion theft
finance_brief.summary: Binance says attackers used malware, bogus recruiter interviews and a compromised internal AI tool to reach its wallet systems before the Oct. 29 theft. The company says $2.85 billion of the $6.34 billion taken was frozen or intercepted, and the FBI blames North Korea, which denies it.
